title: Scheduled polls use a stale focus-state snapshot
author: OskarEichler
body_preview: ### Problem  `startNextPoll` reads `const state = api.getState()[reducerPath]` when it schedules a timeout, then the timeout callback checks `state.config.focused`. Redux state is immutable, so that callback keeps the focus value from scheduling time rather than the value when the poll actually fires. title: Completed retry backoffs retain abort listeners
author: OskarEichler
body_preview: ### Problem  `defaultBackoff` adds a one-shot listener to the request signal for every retry delay. When the timer wins, that listener is never removed because `{ once: true }` only cleans it up if the abort event actually fires. A long-lived signal therefore retains one closure per completed backoff until it is eventually aborted or collected.  With repeated retries this unnecessarily retains tim...

title: resetApiState leaves the pending subscription sync timer running
author: OskarEichler
body_preview: ### Problem  The batched subscription handler sets `updateSyncTimer = null` when handling `resetApiState`, but does not clear the existing 500ms timeout. The old callback still runs after reset, serializes current internal subscriptions, dispatches `subscriptionsUpdated`, and writes `updateSyncTimer = null` again. title: A tag with a falsy ID is never invalidated
author: petr-kratochvil
body_preview: ### Summary  When a tag has a falsy ID, it is treated as _without ID_ on writing, but as _with ID_ on read and cleanup.  Consequences: - The tag is never effectivelly invalidated by such ID - The stale query references accumulate (instead of being cleaned up after unsubscribe)  ### Minimal reproduction  Tested on: "@reduxjs/toolkit": "2.12.0". title: Falsy query errors disable retryOnMount when throwOnError returns false
author: jeonghoon11
body_preview: ### Describe the bug  When a query rejects with a falsy value such as `undefined`, it does not retry on remount even though `retryOnMount` is `true` and `throwOnError` returns `false`.  The condition that handles function-valued `throwOnError` checks the truthiness of `query.state.error`.
